job.title: CDL Driver
job.description:
The JobSquad Solutions Team is currently looking for a CDL Driver  to work at a company located in the Rogers, AR area!

Job Title: CDL Driver

 

Job Location: Rogers 

 

Pay and Hours for Job + Benefits: Up to $26/hr, Mon-Fri 6:30AM-4PM 

 

Position Summary: CDL Driver that is dependable, safety conscious. The driver will be responsible for safely operating company commercial motor vehicles, including standard manual transmission trucks—to transport scrap materials, roll-off containers, or structural steel products between our facility, local suppliers, and customer locations  

 

Key Responsibilities:  

Transport Operations: Safely drive and operate commercial trucks (such as roll-offs, flatbeds, or tractor-trailers), utilizing manual transmissions to navigate various road and yard conditions. 

 

Route Management: Navigate local and regional routes efficiently while strictly adhering to all Department of Transportation (DOT) rules, local traffic laws, and company safety guidelines. 

 

Loading & Unloading: Assist with or manage the secure loading, tarping, and unloading of materials, ensuring proper weight distribution and securement using chains, binders, or straps. 

 

Container Service: Drop off, pick up, and position roll-off or storage containers at commercial and industrial customer sites as requested. 

 

Vehicle Inspections: Conduct thorough pre-trip and post-trip inspections of the vehicle and equipment, documenting any mechanical issues or maintenance needs immediately. 

 

Yard Support: Assist with general scrap yard operations, material sorting, or equipment loading when not driving. 

Position Requirements:  

License: Valid Commercial Driver’s License (Class A or Class B CDL depending on assigned fleet equipment) without an airbrake restriction. 

 

Manual Transmission Proficiency: Required. Must have proven, hands-on experience and proficiency in operating heavy-duty commercial vehicles with manual transmissions (e.g., 8-speed, 9-speed, 10-speed, or similar shift patterns) without relying on automatic-only restrictions. 

 

Experience: Minimum 1–2 years of verifiable commercial driving experience; prior experience in the recycling, construction, or heavy-haul industry is strongly preferred. 

 

Certifications: Must maintain a valid DOT medical card and pass a pre-employment drug screen and background check. 

 

Physical Demands: Ability to sit for long periods, operate a clutch and manual shifter repeatedly, walk on uneven scrap-yard surfaces, climb ladders/stairs on trucks and trailers, and regularly lift up to 50 lbs.  

 

If you have any questions regarding this position, please reach out:

job.title: Maintenance Technician - 2nd Shift
job.description:
The JobSquad Solutions Team is currently looking for a Maintenance Technician - 2nd Shift  to work at a company located in the Bedford Park, IL area!

Job Title: Maintenance Technician - 2nd Shift  
 
Job Location: Bedford Park, IL 60638
 
Pay and Hours for Job + Benefits: 
Pay: $34.00-$40.00 per hour depending on experience plus overtime pay
Hours: 1:30pm-10:00pm 
 
Benefits: 
  1. Healthcare coverage including medical, dental and vision
  2. 401k Plan
  3. Short term disability available
  4. Paid holidays, vacation and paid sick leave
 
Job Description:
 
About the Role
The Maintenance Technician is responsible for ensuring the efficient operation and maintenance of machinery and mechanical equipment in the production facility. This role focuses on minimizing downtime, maintaining quality standards, and supporting the production team by performing timely repairs, adjustments, and preventive maintenance.

  Key Responsibilities:
 
  • Perform setup, repair, and maintenance of production machinery, including ovens, packing lines, and conveyors, ensuring optimal performance and minimal downtime.
  • Conduct routine inspections and preventive maintenance to identify potential issues before they impact production.
  • Troubleshoot mechanical, electrical, and pneumatic systems to resolve equipment malfunctions quickly and effectively.
  • Repair and maintain plumbing systems, hydraulic components, and cutting tools to support facility operations.
  • Operate and maintain power tools and industrial equipment safely, adhering to all safety protocols.
  • Perform welding tasks (MIG, TIG, Stick) to repair or fabricate machine components as needed.
  • Diagnose and troubleshoot PLC (Programmable Logic Controller) systems and electrical issues to maintain automation systems.
  • Document maintenance activities, including repairs and inspections, ensuring accurate records for compliance and future reference.
  • Collaborate with the production team to minimize disruptions and improve operational efficiency.
  • Support changeovers by preparing and adjusting equipment to meet production requirements.
  • Ensure compliance with GMP (Good Manufacturing Practices), safety protocols, and food industry regulations.  
 
Qualifications:
 
  • High school diploma or equivalent; technical certification or degree is a plus.
  • 2-5 years of experience in an industrial bakery and/or food manufacturing environment preferred.
  • Strong mechanical and troubleshooting skills with a service-oriented mindset.
  • Experience with equipment maintenance, including conveyors, pneumatic systems, and hydraulics. Power Industrial Training Certification is a plus. Proficiency in electrical systems and PLC diagnostics is highly desirable.
  • Welding experience (MIG, TIG, Stick) is a significant advantage. Must be a self-starter capable of working independently and completing projects without supervision. Excellent communication skills and ability to work effectively in a team environment.
  • Bilingual (English/Spanish) is a plus but not required.

job.title: Bilingual Maintenance Technician
job.description:
The JobSquad Solutions Team is currently looking for a Bilingual Maintenance Technician to work at a company located in the New Haven, CT area!

Job Title:  Bilingual Maintenance Technician
 
Job Location: New Haven, CT
 
Pay and Hours for Job + Benefits We are hiring an experienced Bilingual Maintenance Technician for a food manufacturing facility in New Haven, CT. This is a full-time, hands-on maintenance position responsible for keeping production equipment operating safely and efficiently while minimizing downtime.
What You'll Do
  • Troubleshoot, repair, and maintain industrial production and packaging equipment.
  • Perform mechanical repairs on conveyors, motors, gearboxes, pumps, bearings, and related equipment.
  • Respond to equipment breakdowns and make timely repairs to minimize production downtime.
  • Perform scheduled preventive maintenance and document completed work in a CMMS system.
  • Inspect equipment for wear, leaks, unusual noise, and other potential problems.
  • Troubleshoot pneumatic and hydraulic systems and mechanical power transmission equipment.
  • Support facility systems including piping, HVAC components, lighting, and compressed air.
  • Assist with refrigeration, boiler, and water systems as qualified.
  • Perform basic electrical troubleshooting, including sensors, electrical schematics, and use of a multimeter.
  • Participate in root-cause analysis and recommend improvements to prevent recurring equipment failures.
  • Follow OSHA, SQF, food safety, and Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) requirements.
  • Work closely with production personnel to troubleshoot equipment and improve reliability.
Requirements
  • 3–5 years of industrial maintenance or industrial mechanic experience in a manufacturing environment.
  • Bilingual in English and Spanish.
  • Strong mechanical troubleshooting and repair skills.
  • Experience with conveyors, motors, bearings, pumps, pneumatics, hydraulics, and mechanical power transmission.
  • Ability to read blueprints, mechanical drawings, and equipment manuals.
  • Proficiency with hand tools, power tools, and precision measuring equipment.
  • Working knowledge of CMMS systems.
  • Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to work safely under time-sensitive conditions.
  • Basic electrical skills, including reading schematics, replacing sensors, and using a multimeter.
  • Food manufacturing experience is strongly preferred but not required.
Preferred Experience
  • Experience in an SQF- or USDA-regulated food manufacturing facility.
  • Welding and fabrication experience, including MIG/TIG, cutting, and grinding.
  • Trade school, technical certification, apprenticeship, or other formal industrial maintenance training.
Physical Requirements
  • Ability to stand, walk, climb, kneel, bend, and work on your feet for extended periods.
  • Routinely lift, carry, push, and pull up to 50 lbs; occasionally up to 75 lbs.
  • Comfortable working around moving machinery, vibration, wet conditions, cleaning chemicals, and food-processing equipment.
  • Ability to work in varying temperatures, including cold rooms and warm processing areas.
  • Ability to wear required PPE, including steel-toe shoes, hearing protection, and eye protection.

What We're Looking For
The ideal candidate is a dependable, hands-on maintenance professional who can diagnose problems quickly, make quality repairs, and take a proactive approach to preventing equipment failures. Food manufacturing experience is a plus, but strong industrial maintenance experience is the priority.
Pay: $28.50–$29.50/hour
Monday–Friday | 3:00 PM–11:30 PM
Full-Time | New Haven, CT
English/Spanish Bilingual Required

job.description:
The JobSquad Solutions Team is currently looking for a Accounting Clerk  to work at a company located in the Gravette, AR area!

Job Title: Accounting Clerk 

 

Job Location: Gravette 

 

Pay and Hours for Job + Benefits: Up to $18/hr, Mon-Fri 8AM-5PM 

 

Position Summary: 

The Accounting Clerk is responsible for providing comprehensive accounting support by computing, classifying, and recording numerical data to maintain accurate financial records. This position manages the full cycle of accounts payable and accounts receivable, ensuring files are complete, payments are processed timely, and customer/vendor accounts remain in good standing. The Accounting Clerk provides high-level support to accounting supervisors, managers, and other department staff to ensure the integrity of the company’s financial operations. 

 

Key Responsibilities:  

Perform accounting and clerical functions to support supervisors; research, track, and resolve  complex accounting problems and discrepancies.  

Code and input data (invoices, checks, account statements, reports) into financial processing  systems according to company procedures; work in QuickBooks to support the company.  

Review A/P for accuracy and ensure proper approvals are in place; process credit cards  payable and accounts payable to ensure payments are current; audit bills against purchase orders.  

Generate and distribute customer invoices, credit memos, internal sales orders, and account  statements; add, receive, and post customer payments and credits to specific accounts.  

Manage the collections process for past-due accounts, conferring with customers to resolve  payment delays; audit invoices against purchase orders and research discrepancies.  

Prepare checks, account statements, and reports; assist with project and job cost reporting;  reconcile report discrepancies and assist with expense report tracking.  

Compile and sort documents (bills, checks, purchase orders) substantiating business  transactions; maintain digital and physical records by scanning and filing.  

Assist employees, vendors, clients, or customers by answering questions related to accounts,  procedures, and services.  

Assist with licensing compliance and other regulatory documentation.  

Assist with special projects and perform other job-related duties as assigned.

job.title: Transportation Operations Analyst
job.description:
The JobSquad Solutions Team is currently looking for a Transportation Operations Analyst  to work at a company located in the Miami, FL area!

Job Title: Transportation Operations Analyst  
 
Job Location: Miami, FL 33172
 
Pay and Hours for Job + Benefits: $60k per year
 
Job Description: 
Transportation Operations Analyst is responsible for supporting and optimizing domestic and international transportation activities supporting Uplift operations, repair shipments to and from repair shops, and ad hoc logistics requirements. The role manages shipment booking, tracking, transportation vendors, customs coordination, and freight cost and service analysis to ensure aircraft material moves safely, compliantly, on time, and at the right cost. This position serves as a key transportation liaison across Operations, Uplift, Repairs, Warehouse, Quality, Finance, and external carriers, freight forwarders, and customs brokers.
  
Key accountabilities:
  • Support end-to-end transportation execution for Uplift, Repairs, and ad hoc logistics requests, from initial request and routing decision through final delivery and proof of delivery.
  • Serve as the primary point of accountability for transportation issues, proactively managing priorities, shipment visibility, delays, exceptions, and recovery actions.
  • Manage repair logistics to and from MROs and repair vendors, coordinating pickup, routing, customs requirements, delivery, return movements, and status visibility with the Repairs and Uplift teams.
  • Source, evaluate, qualify, and manage carriers, freight forwarders, couriers, customs brokers, and specialized logistics providers; build a reliable network of preferred partners that can support company’s global and time-critical needs.
  • Negotiate spot rates, contracted rates, discounts, service levels, accessorial charges, and commercial terms with transportation vendors; challenge unnecessary costs and use market benchmarks and shipment data to drive measurable savings.
  • Own vendor performance management, including service reviews, scorecards, escalations, corrective actions, and follow-up on recurring failures; hold partners accountable for agreed service and communication standards.
  • Support transportation RFQs, RFPs, bid events, and contract reviews in partnership with Operations leadership, Finance, and other stakeholders, ensuring commercial decisions balance cost, reliability, speed, and operational risk.
  • Build and maintain transportation standards including routing guides, preferred carrier rules, booking procedures, escalation paths, documentation requirements, and operating playbooks that can scale with company growth.
  • Own transportation cost and performance visibility by monitoring spend, transit performance, on-time delivery, exception rates, claims, and vendor service; develop recurring KPIs and actionable reporting for Operations leadership.
  • Analyze shipment history, carrier performance, routing patterns, and freight costs to identify consolidation opportunities, network changes, service improvements, and cost-reduction initiatives; convert analysis into implemented actions.
  • Partner across Uplift, Repairs, Warehouse, Quality, Finance, Sales, and other teams to anticipate transportation requirements, remove bottlenecks, improve handoffs, and create a consistently high level of internal service.
  • Act as a builder within Operations: identify broken or missing processes, challenge the status quo constructively, create practical solutions, document standards, and drive improvements through to sustained adoption.
  • Model company expected culture through ownership, accountability, responsiveness, collaboration, high standards, and a willingness to remain hands-on when the operation needs support.
Key skills and competences:
  • Strong ownership mindset with the ability to take an ambiguous problem, create a plan, make decisions, and drive it through to resolution.
  • Proven vendor-management capability, including performance reviews, escalation management, corrective actions, and holding external partners accountable.
  • Builder mentality with a demonstrated ability to create processes, standards, reporting, and scalable ways of working rather than simply operate an existing process.
  • Strong analytical skills with a practical understanding of freight cost, routing, transit performance, service trade-offs, and transportation KPIs.
  • Ability to influence across functions and manage stakeholders without relying on formal authority; comfortable working directly with senior leaders and front-line operational teams.
  • Excellent organization and attention to detail across simultaneous shipments, quotations, documentation, customs requirements, and vendor commitments.
  • Clear, concise verbal and written communication, including the ability to provide decisive status updates, commercial recommendations, and escalations.
  • Microsoft Excel capability and comfort working with transportation data, dashboards, ERP/TMS platforms, carrier portals, and process automation tools.
  • Working knowledge of international transportation, import/export processes, customs documentation, Incoterms, and transportation best practices.
Experience and qualifications:
  • Bachelor's or associate’s degree in Logistics, Supply Chain, Transportation, Business Administration, or a related field preferred; equivalent relevant experience will be considered.
  • Minimum 4-6 years of progressive experience in transportation, freight forwarding, international logistics, shipping operations, or supply chain, with demonstrated ownership beyond basic shipment coordination.
  • Experience managing domestic and international parcel, air freight, ground, courier, and time-critical shipments from booking through final delivery.
  • Demonstrated experience negotiating freight rates or commercial terms and managing carrier, freight-forwarder, courier, or customs-broker relationships.
  • Experience building or improving transportation processes, routing guides, vendor scorecards, KPIs, SOPs, or cost-control programs strongly preferred.
  • Working knowledge of import/export documentation, customs-clearance processes, Incoterms, and international shipping requirements.
  • Strong Microsoft Excel skills; experience with ERP systems, TMS platforms, carrier portals, BI/reporting tools, or transportation automation preferred.
  • Experience in aviation, aerospace, MRO, aircraft-parts distribution, or another high-value, time-critical technical distribution environment preferred.
  • Knowledge of ATA Spec 300 packaging requirements preferred; hazmat / IATA Dangerous Goods training or certification is a plus.

Job Description: 
Our client is seeking for an Accounting Coordinator to join their freight forward organization in Miami Lakes, FL.
Are you a detail-oriented finance professional who thrives in the fast-paced world of international logistics? We are looking for an Accounting Coordinator with freight forwarding experience to join our collaborative team in Miami Lakes! If you love keeping the numbers in check while supporting dynamic daily trade operations, we’d love to meet you.

What You’ll Do
You will serve as a vital pillar of our financial operations, partnering closely with our Accounting, Operations, and Management teams to ensure all vendor payments, customer invoices, freight charges, and financial transactions run smoothly.

 
  • Accounts Payable (AP): Review, code, and enter vendor invoices for ocean, air, trucking, warehousing, and customs services. Match invoices against rate agreements, POs, and shipment records while verifying transport-specific fees (demurrage, storage, detention, and terminal charges).
 
  • Accounts Receivable (AR) & Billing: Generate and dispatch accurate customer billing, process incoming payments, and follow up gently on outstanding account balances.
 
  • Reconciliations & Closing: Perform bank reconciliations, assist with month-end closing activities, and ensure financial records align perfectly with operational documentation.
 
  • Cross-Department Support: Collaborate with the operations team to resolve billing discrepancies and keep shipment records moving forward without friction.
 
What We’re Looking For

 
  • Industry Experience: Prior experience in freight forwarding, ocean/air shipping, transportation, or logistics is highly preferred.
 
  • Core Accounting Skills: Proven hands-on experience in AP, AR, billing, and general ledger coding.
 
  • Detail & Efficiency: High accuracy when handling transport documentation, rate sheets, and high-volume data entry under deadlines.
 
  • Team Mindset: Strong communication skills and a collaborative attitude to work alongside internal teams and external logistics partners.

Job Description:
A CNC Machinist sets up, programs, and operates computer-controlled machinery to cut, shape, and finish precision metal and plastic parts.
  1. Read Blueprints: Interpret technical drawings, schematics, and CAD/CAM files to understand exact part dimensions.
  2. Setup and Program: Install cutting tools, secure raw materials, and input programs to guide machine operations.
  3. Monitor and Inspect: Oversee production runs and use precision measuring tools like calipers to check that finished parts match specifications.
  4. Troubleshoot: Fix minor machine errors, adjust speeds and feeds, and perform routine equipment maintenance.
  5. Operator: Focuses on loading parts, running cycles, and basic quality checks.
  6. Machinist: Handles more complex programming, advanced machine setup, and troubleshooting.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor (Food Company)
job.description:
The JobSquad Solutions Team is currently looking for a Maintenance Supervisor (Food Company) to work at a company located in the Alma, GA area!

Job Title:  Maintenance Supervisor (Food Company)
 
Job Location:  Alma, GA 31510
 
Compensation:  $75,000-$90,000 base plus bonus 
 
Hours:  7:00am-4:00pm (Monday-Friday)
 
 
Company Benefits: 
 
Low-cost comprehensive health, dental, and vision insurance, a wellness program with paycheck incentives, 401(k) matching, paid time off, and on-the-job career development
 
 
 
JOB DESCRIPTION  
 
Summary
The Maintenance Supervisor is responsible for supervising and coordinating activities of employees engaged in maintaining and repairing building structures, grounds, utilities, and critical processing systems within a USDA-regulated meat processing facility. This role ensures safe, reliable, sanitary, and compliant operation of refrigeration, building, and utility systems while supporting food safety, employee safety, and production requirements.
Essential Duties and Responsibilities
  • Supervise, coordinate, and participate in maintenance activities involving building structures, grounds, utilities, and processing areas.
  • Direct employees performing structural maintenance including masonry, carpentry, painting, and equipment support.
  • Oversee electrical maintenance including motor controls, high and low voltage wiring, and PLC-supported systems.
  • Provide sanitation-support maintenance ensuring hygienic repairs and prevention of product contamination.
  • Plan, schedule, and execute preventive and corrective maintenance activities to minimize downtime.
  • Inspect completed work for conformance with specifications, food safety requirements, and regulatory standards.
  • Maintain accurate maintenance records, work orders, inspections, and inventory using the ERP system.
  • Request, manage, and control tools, equipment, spare parts, and maintenance supplies.
  • Analyze maintenance problems, determine root causes, and implement corrective actions.
  • Interpret company policies and enforce safety, food safety, and sanitation regulations.
  • Recommend improvements in equipment, procedures, and working conditions to improve safety and efficiency.
  • Assist other departments as requested, including equipment moves, installations, and special projects.
  • Remain on-call and respond to emergency maintenance situations as required.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.
Food Safety & Regulatory Compliance
  • Ensure all maintenance activities comply with USDA, FSIS, OSHA, EPA, and local regulations.
  • Support HACCP plans and maintenance-related Critical Control Points (CCPs).
  • Prevent chemical, physical, and biological contamination resulting from maintenance activities.
  • Participate in USDA inspections, internal audits, and third-party audits.
  • Ensure proper release of equipment and areas following maintenance prior to production startup.
  • Maintain compliance with sanitation standard operating procedures (SSOPs).
Refrigeration, Utilities & PSM Responsibilities
  • Supervise the operation and maintenance of ammonia refrigeration systems in compliance with PSM and RMP requirements.
  • Hold or maintain RETA Class A operator certification as required. If candidate does not hold the certification, he will be required to take the license in less than a year from hire date.
  • Serve as part of the facility emergency response team for ammonia and utility-related incidents.
  • Ensure completion of required PSM documentation, inspections, and training.
Contractor & Vendor Management
  • Assist Maintenance Manager in oversight of outside contractors and service providers.
  • Ensure contractors comply with food safety, safety, and regulatory requirements.
  • Assist Maintenance Manager in reviewing permits, credentials, and work scope prior to authorizing work.
  • Assist Maintenance Manager monitor contractor performance and costs.
Supervisory Responsibilities
Directly supervises maintenance employees. Responsibilities include interviewing, hiring, training, planning and assigning work, evaluating performance, rewarding and disciplining employees, and resolving conflicts in accordance with company policies and applicable laws.
Qualifications
  • High school diploma or GED required; technical or trade schooling preferred.
  • Four years of experience in an industrial or meat processing maintenance environment.
  • Minimum five years' operating ammonia refrigeration system; two years as lead technician preferred.
  • Working knowledge of electrical systems, motor controls, and PLC-supported equipment.
  • Knowledge of OSHA, EPA, USDA, and PSM regulatory requirements.

The Quality Control Inspector- Ensures aviation articles meet manufacturer and operator specifications, including Dimensions, condition, operational limits, and compliance with the company’s Quality Management System. This role is critical in maintaining adherence to quality procedures, customer requirements, and regulatory standards set by federal and other governing agencies.
 
 Essential Job Functions:
  • Conduct thorough inspections using various methods to assess product airworthiness.
  • Interpret engineering publications, shop travelers, FAA regulations, and manufacturer technical data and drawings to define inspection scope.
  • Determine optimal inspection techniques and sequence of operations.
  • Use precision measuring instruments to verify part dimensions, tolerances, and clearances.

  • Support other inspectors and technicians through mentoring and guidance.
  • Collaborate with management and planning teams to prioritize tasks.
  • Monitor compliance with 14 CFR Part 145, Part 21 and the FAA-approved Repair Station/Quality Control Manual.
  • Perform additional duties as assigned by the Quality Control Manager or Chief Inspector.
 
 Requirements:

This is a hands-on Assembly role in a structured manufacturing environment involving injection molding and production operations. The role requires strong attention to detail, adherence to safety and quality standards, and the ability to work consistently at required production rates.
Physical & Environmental Requirements
  • This is a standing position for the entire shift, except for two paid breaks and one 15-minute unpaid lunch. No seating is available at the press. 
  • Frequent walking, reaching, and use of hands is required. 
  • Occasional bending, climbing, or crouching may be necessary. 
  • Must be able to regularly lift and/or move 35–50 pounds. 
  • Requires good overall vision, including close, distance, color, and depth perception. 
  • Work environment includes moving machinery, moderate noise levels, and occasional exposure to heat, fumes, or airborne particles. 
Skills & Qualifications
  • Prior injection molding experience is preferred; required training must be successfully completed. 
  • Ability to read, understand, and follow safety rules, work instructions, quality standards, and procedures. 
  • Basic computer, communication, math, and problem-solving skills are required. 
  • Ability to follow written, verbal, and diagram-based instructions in a structured environment. 
Key Responsibilities
  • Review inspection plans, work instructions, quality alerts, and control samples before starting production. 
  • Follow all safety rules, procedures, and customer requirements at all times. 
  • Maintain required production rates and work speed consistently. 
  • Inspect, pack, and label parts correctly according to standards. 
  • Record production data accurately (e.g., counts, scrap, labels, etc.). 
  • Maintain 5S standards, including keeping the workstation clean and organized. 
  • Communicate production or quality concerns promptly to supervisors, quality staff, and coworkers. 
  • Report problems or quality issues immediately when they occur. 
  • Support and assist other areas or team members when needed. 
  • Help train new employees on job tasks, quality expectations, 5S practices, and production requirements.

job.title: Road Construction Flagger
job.description:
The JobSquad Solutions Team is currently looking for a Road Construction Flagger  to work at a company located in the Grand Rapids, MI area!

Job Title: 
Road Construction Flagger 
 
Job Location: 
Statewide Hiring Locations: Ann Arbor, Battle Creek, Grand Rapids, Kalamazoo, Lansing, Jackson, Mount Pleasant
 
Pay and Hours for Job + Benefits:
Hourly rate is based on the one-way distance from your home office to the assigned job site, calculated using the shortest available route in Google Maps.
  • 0–49 miles: $20.00/hour
  • 50–79 miles: $21.00/hour
  • 80–99 miles: $22.00/hour
  • 100+ miles: $27.00/hour 
 
 
Job Description:                                                          
 
What the Job Looks Like
  • Schedules are shared daily through our dispatch app (Assignar), by 7:00 PM each night.
  • Shifts typically range from 4 to 14 hours, depending on weather and project needs. (Not including travel time)
  • Work sites change daily. Statewide travel is required.
  • Overtime opportunities are available.
  • Because of the nature of roadwork, scheduled breaks aren’t always guaranteed—but we do our best to make sure you get rest when site conditions allow.
 
 
What You’ll Need
  • Valid driver’s license
  • Reliable personal vehicle (must remain on-site during your shift)
  • Proof of auto insurance (in your name/listed as an insured driver)
  • Availability for full days (sunrise to sunset), including weekends.
  • Ability to work outdoors in all weather conditions.
  • No OWI/DUI within the past 5 years
  • Ability to pass a background check and drug screening.
  • Willingness to travel up to 100+ miles one way.
 
No experience? No problem. We provide training and safety equipment.
 
As a flagger, you’re an important part of keeping both workers and drivers safe. Your responsibilities include:
  • Controlling traffic through construction zones
  • Guiding drivers safely around work areas
  • Using signs, paddles, radios, and hand signals
  • Communicating with your team to keep traffic flowing smoothly.
 
PPE Provided by JobSquad:
  • Safety vest (MDOT Class 3)
  • Safety glasses (clear & tinted)
  • Hard hat
  • Sign & Poles
  • Headlamp
  • 2-way radio (you provide batteries)
  • Poncho
 
You’ll need to bring:
  • T-shirt or long-sleeved shirt (no tank tops)
  • Steel-toed leather boots (ankle coverage required)
  • Durable jeans or work pants (no shorts or sweatpants)
 
We’ve got you covered with a full range of benefits, including:
  • Health, dental, and vision insurance
  • Life and disability coverage
Plus, we offer a $100 referral bonus for every friend you bring on board—no limit.
 
Text “FLAG” to 269-279-7222 to apply!
 

The JobSquad Solutions Team is made up of experts around the country. Serving our local workforce communities is our passion.

  • Oversees all aspects of the day-to-day operations of the manufacturing department.

  • Provides day-to-day leadership to the manufacturing operators and personnel and strives to meet all quality goals.

  • Collaborate with senior management to align production goals with company objectives.
  • Proven track record of improving production efficiency and reducing costs.

  • Must have at least 4 to 6 years of manufacturing supervisory skills in a CGMP environment or manufacturing facility.
  • Must possess strong interpersonal, written, and oral communication skills.
  • Must demonstrate the ability to lead and motivate others effectively.
  • Must have strong organizational abilities and product line analysis.

  • Experience with statistical process control.
  • Experience with world-class manufacturing methods.

  • Ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment.
  • Strong leadership and team management skills.

Job Description:
 
This role involves preparing molds, mixing and pouring matrix materials, curing products, and performing final inspections. It requires strong attention to detail, adherence to safety standards, and the ability to perform hands‑on production tasks, including buffing.

Requirements
Education & Experience
  • High school diploma or equivalent; technical training or certification is a plus.
  • Previous experience in a manufacturing or production environment preferred but not required.
  • REQUIRED: Previous buffing experience.
Skills & Abilities
  • Ability to follow detailed instructions and standard operating procedures.
  • Proficiency with hand tools, power tools, and testing devices.
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to high‑quality output.
  • Basic math and reading comprehension skills.
Physical Requirements
  • Ability to lift and move up to 50 lbs.
  • Able to stand for extended periods and perform repetitive motions.
Personal Attributes
  • Strong work ethic and reliability.
  • Good problem‑solving skills and ability to troubleshoot minor equipment issues.
  • Team‑oriented mindset with effective communication skills.
Safety & Compliance
  • Consistent adherence to all safety regulations and protocols.
  • Commitment to maintaining a clean, organized, and hazard‑free work environment.
Responsibilities
1. Clean and Prepare Molds
  • Inspect molds for residue, defects, or damage.
  • Clean thoroughly using appropriate solvents and tools.
2. Mix Matrix Materials
  • Gather all required components (resin, hardener, fillers, etc.).
  • Follow manufacturer mixing ratios and guidelines.
  • Mix thoroughly—mechanically or by hand—until fully homogeneous.
3. Pour Matrix into Molds
  • Pour from one side to reduce air bubbles and ensure even fill.
  • Tap or gently vibrate molds to release trapped air if needed.
  • Level the surface before curing begins.
4. Curing Process
  • Maintain recommended temperature and humidity conditions.
  • Allow full curing time as specified for the material.
5. Demolding & Final Inspection
  • Carefully remove cured parts by flexing molds as needed.
  • Inspect finished pieces for imperfections and perform touch‑ups if required.
